title: lazy-reservation-and-slab-fractioning-for-paged-kv
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces lazy commit reservations and slab fractioning for the paged KV block manager. Improves memory reuse and reduces write amplification; no API changes.
body:
Context and motivation:
The paged KV block manager currently conservatively reserves commit tokens and prefers whole-slab reclamation. For workloads with high locality and many short-lived prefixes (e.g., prefix caching for multi-tenant chat sessions), this leads to two observable inefficiencies: (1) transient reservations that hold slab capacity but never get dirtied, and (2) coarse-grained slab eviction that prevents intra-slab reuse, increasing churn and IO writeback.

Summary of changes (single-line bullets for quick scanning):
- Add lazy reservation tokens: only convert a soft-reservation into a committed reservation when a write actually occurs. Soft-reservations are tracked cheaply and do not increment commit counters that block slab reuse.
- Implement slab fractioning: allow a slab to be split into 2/4 logical fractions for allocation/reuse to increase packing density for small hot pages. Fractioning happens at allocation time; fractions can be coalesced lazily when full-slab reuse is needed.
- Background coalescer: lightweight background worker that coalesces adjacent free fractions into full slabs during low load windows to keep fragmentation bounded.
- Metrics and tracing: new paged_kv.lazy_reserve_hit/miss, paged_kv.fraction_alloc_count, paged_kv.coalesce_cycles gauges and histograms. Added debug traces for reservation->commit lifecycle.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests covering race cases for lazy commit, integration test to ensure crash-safety under uncommitted-soft-reservations, and end-to-end perf harness with internal microbenchmarks.

Detailed description (technical):
Lazy reservation semantics: introduce two reservation types: soft_reservation (cheap, can be dropped) and hard_commit (previously just reservation). Soft reservations are recorded in a small per-shard bloom-ish bitmap and a lightweight refcount. When a caller performs the first written mutation to that block, we atomically promote the soft_reservation to a hard_commit (path guarded by existing commit_mutex to preserve consistency). This avoids incrementing global committed_block counters for read-only or canceled reservations.

Slab fractioning design: slabs remain the same underlying physical unit (4MB by default) but now may be logically partitioned into 2 or 4 fractions based on historical allocation size histograms. The allocator uses a new heuristic: if >60% of recent allocations in a shard are <256KB, prefer 4-way fractioning; otherwise 2-way or no fractioning. Fraction metadata is stored in the existing slab header extension (24 bytes) to avoid additional mallocs and keep on-disk layout compatible. Coalescing metadata is versioned so older on-disk slabs are still readable.

Background coalescer: single threaded per-N shards, rate-limited task that runs when (1) CPU idle < 30% and (2) free_fraction_ratio > 0.5. Coalescer merges adjacent free fractions into larger free spans to reduce fragmentation long-term. Coalescing uses epoch-safe reclamation so normal request paths do not need stop-the-world pauses.

Safety and crash recovery: soft reservations are only persisted as ephemeral metadata in-memory and not written to on-disk slab headers. To guard against lost soft reservations on process restart, the allocator treats any partially-occupied fraction as free and lets the background recovery pass revalidate contents via checksums (unchanged from existing recovery flow). Hard commits still have the same on-disk commit markers.

Benchmarks and results (internal perf harness, measuring steady-state serving with mixed read/write prefix workloads):
- Small-prefix 80/20 read/write workload (tenants=200): average memory fragmentation down by 22%, cache hit effective capacity +14% (measured by evictions), host CPU for allocation path down 8%.
- Mixed-batch inference workload (continuation-heavy KV hits): 95th percentile latency for token-serving path reduced by 6.2ms (approx 4.3% at 95p), p50 no-regression.
- Writeback IO: write amplification reduced ~9% in microbench test due to better packing of hot pages.

Commits (high-level):
- feat: add soft_reservation + promotion logic (allocator/*.cc, runtime/kv_shard.h)
- feat: slab fractioning allocator and headers (allocator/slab_fraction.cc, allocator/slab_header.h)
- fix: coalescer worker and rate limiter (allocator/coalescer.cc)
- perf: add metrics and traces (observability/paged_kv_metrics.{cc,h})
- test: unit + integration + perf harness updates (test/kv_lazy_reserve_test.cc, test/coalesce_integration.cc)

Files changed (high level):
- allocator/slab_pool.cc (new fractioning heuristics, ~+230/-34)
- allocator/slab_fraction.cc (new, +410)
- allocator/slab_header.h (+24 bytes to header)
- allocator/coalescer.cc (+142)
- runtime/kv_shard.h (+60)
- runtime/kv_reservation.{cc,h} (+120)
- observability/paged_kv_metrics.cc (+48)
- test/kv_lazy_reserve_test.cc (+95)
- test/coalesce_integration.cc (+170)
- benchmarks/paged_kv_pack_density.py (+85)
- docs/ops/paged-kv-adm.md (docs +60)
- build/BUCK / CMakeLists tweaks (+/-)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Diego Martinez (reviewer): "Nice approach. Concern: are we underestimating the memory overhead for per-shard soft bitmaps? Can we quantify worst-case?"
- Author (Asha): "Answered: worst-case bitmap per-shard ~128KB (default config) and we add a knob paged_kv.soft_reserve_bitmap_bytes. Added microbench numbers + memory column. If customers need to reduce, setting to 32KB still keeps >95% of benefits in our tests."
- Priya Nair: "We need an explicit abort path for promoted reservation failures (OOM) so callers don't assume commit success."
- Author: "Added abort semantics: promotion returns an error and the calling txn can fail cleanly; documented in runtime/kv_reservation.h and surfaced in the unit tests."
- Liam O'Connor: "Integration looks solid. Please add an observability dashboard tile for fraction utilization."
- Author: "Added dashboard JSON and linked in docs/ops/paged-kv-adm.md."

CI and validation: all unit tests passing; integration job 'kv-integration-large' passing after one rerun (flake on network mount); perf job ran with new harness and results attached in artifacts/perf/129876/results.zip. Fuzzer did not find races in our promotion path after 48h.

Merge strategy and outcome:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Merge commit message appended to change log with short benchmark summary.

Follow-ups and known limitations:
- This patch slightly increases CPU for background coalescer under very high churn if fractioning is over-aggressive; added an opt-out flag (paged_kv.enable_fractioning=false) and dynamic telemetry to flip heuristics server-side in the short term.
- Long-term: consider multi-size fractioning (e.g., 8-way) and adaptive fraction lifetime informed by TTL signals from upper layers. Filed ENG-1229 for follow-up exploration.

Checklist (as part of PR description):
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added that simulate crash/restart
- [x] Benchmarks added to perf harness
- [x] Docs/ops page updated
- [x] Metrics and tracing added

If you want to run locally: checkout branch, run `bazel test //test:kv_lazy_reserve_test` and `python3 benchmarks/paged_kv_pack_density.py --runs 20`.

If any reviewer wants a walkthrough I can present perf harness results and show a flamegraph for the allocation hot path.
